title: fix(#6651): cross-realm is not a wont-fix — seed four intrinsics on the realm global (+11 ES2015 standalone rows)
author: claude
head: 3798acc710cd706456ede71ed60517ab2bbb880e
body:
## Description

**Before:** `$262.createRealm().global.Symbol` answered `undefined` in standalone, so every ES2015 `cross-realm` row that reads a well-known symbol off the foreign realm died before its assertion. The cluster table in the issue file recorded this whole bucket as the *"clearest wont-fix-with-reason group in the cluster"* — a standalone binary is one realm by construction, so there is nothing to fix.

**After:** the four missing names are seeded on the realm global, eleven ES2015 `cross-realm` rows pass, and the wont-fix is struck through as superseded. The reasoning behind it was wrong.

### The recorded cause was wrong

`$262` is **not** a host object in this lane. It is ordinary JavaScript compiled into the module from `scripts/test262-fyi-runtime.js`, and its `createRealm()` returns a plain object that forwards ten real intrinsics off `globalThis` and mints seven distinct error constructors. The foreign realm already exists, and **39 of 128 rows already passed**. This is ordinary compiler work, not an architectural impossibility.

(The `wrapTest` legacy preamble in `tests/test262-runner.ts` has a *different* `createRealm` returning an empty object. That is not the shim that runs — the authoritative lane goes through `assembleOriginalHarness`.)

### How

Probed on the base commit: one standalone module reading `{ X: globalThis.X }` for 21 builtin names. Seventeen answered a real carrier and exactly `Symbol`, `ArrayBuffer`, `DataView` and `Promise` answered null — while `Symbol`, `{S:Symbol}.S` and `{S:Symbol}.S.iterator === Symbol.iterator` all already worked. **The carrier was never missing; the realm object's property was.** All four are in `BUILTIN_CONSTRUCTOR_IDENTITY_NAMES`, so the value seeded is the same `__builtin_ctor_<Name>` singleton the bare read produces — this closes a split between two spellings of one intrinsic rather than minting a second.

The half that mattered: adding the names to the existing `STANDALONE_GLOBAL_CONSTRUCTOR_NAMES` moved **zero** rows. `appendStandaloneGlobalConstructorSeeds` early-returns for any module with a runtime-eval boundary site, and every test262 module carrying the `$262` shim also carries its `evalScript` — so that return always fires. The four live in a separate list seeded on **both** sides of the gate. The gate's stated hazard is `%Function%` parity re-entry, which these four are outside of; they do not overlap the existing list.

## Measurements

**ES2015 cross-realm, standalone, `--isolate`, 128 rows, per-PATH set diff:** 39 pass → 50 pass, **+11, −0**, no other verdict changed, 0 CE and 0 `error` on both sides. The eleven are the `built-ins/Symbol/<well-known>/cross-realm.js` family. `Symbol/for` and `Symbol/keyFor` correctly did *not* flip — they need a genuinely distinct realm.

**Regression sweep, 1,680 rows** (`built-ins/{Symbol,ArrayBuffer,DataView,Promise,global}/**` + `language/global-code/**`), standalone, `--isolate`: **+20, 0 pass rows lost** against CI's published standalone baseline. Five gains outside cross-realm are the same defect from the other side (`verifyProperty(this,'<Name>')`). Three apparent `fail→compile_error` rows reproduce identically with the change reverted, so they are local drift, not this branch.

**Regression test** `tests/issue-6651-x1-realm-global-ctor-seeds.test.ts`: 3/3 red with the source file reverted to base, 3/3 green restored. Verified independently a second time by the integrating session, reverting the file and re-running.

## Feasibility verdict for the rest of the bucket

Of the 89 failures, only **30** are standalone-lowering gaps — 59 fail on host too and belong to the shared front-end. Forty rows read a name the shim does not forward at all (`Object` 17, `RegExp` 7, `String` 6, …) and die on `undefined.<prop>`.

**Sixteen rows require a genuinely distinct realm** (per-realm intrinsic tables, a realm field on every function object for `GetFunctionRealm`, realm-aware error construction, plus a harness minting a real second global — five subsystems). So the honest ceiling for this bucket without realm isolation is **112/128 (88%)**, not 100%. The biggest remaining lever is `proto-from-ctor-realm` semantics (~45 rows, one mechanism): §9.1.14 GetPrototypeFromConstructor must fall back to the intrinsic default proto when `newTarget.prototype` is not an object.

## Not done

No host-lane sweep — the seed sits behind `if (!ctx.standalone && !ctx.wasi) return;`, so host is byte-inert by construction. **No WASI sweep: the seed is on the same gate as WASI and that lane was not measured.** Stated as residual risk rather than measured away.

Gates run bare, all exit 0: `check-loc-budget` (+30 LOC, no allowance needed), `check-func-budget`, `check-coercion-sites`, `check:oracle-ratchet`, `check:dead-exports`, `check-host-import-policy` (`src/runtime.ts` untouched), `check-compiler-boundaries --mode inventory --base HEAD^1`. No new `src/` file, so no `compiler-boundaries.json` entry needed.

Issue: [#6651](https://js2wasm.loopdive.com/dashboard/issue.html?slug=6651-es2015-standalone-100pct-execution-plan)
